name: sprouts_entity_lookup
description:
Full records for IDENTIFIERS YOU ALREADY HOLD: domains, LinkedIn URLs, names, or record ids. The enrichment tool; do not search for something you can look up.

Say what the ids are with `by`: a company by `domain` or `li_url`, a person by `li_url` (a person has no domain), `name` for either, or `auto` to classify each value. A row from a search or look-alike result carries a `lookup` value: pass its `by` and value, never the row's `id`, which is not a record id and comes back not found.

Every id is answered, in order. `found: false` is a miss: we hold no record under that identifier, which is not proof the entity does not exist. `found: true` with empty `matches` means the record exists but none came back. `ambiguous: true` means several records matched (a name is not a unique key): show them rather than picking the first. At most 3 matches are shown per id. Company and person records are trimmed to a compact default set unless you name `fields`.

Batch ceilings: 1,000 ids for company and person, 50 when `by` is set, 100 for document categories (50 by name). Billed 1 credit per record found; a miss is free. `environment: "test"` in a result means a test key: real records, zero credits.

category.description: Which kind of record to look up. Decides what `by` accepts.

ids.description: The identifiers to resolve: raw values (domains, LinkedIn URLs, names) when `by` is set, record ids when it is not.

by.description: What the ids are. `company`: auto, domain, li_url or name. `person`: auto, li_url or name. `news_article`, `funding_round`, `job_opening`, `market_report`: id (the default) or name (a headline, the funded company, a job title or a report title; one name can match several documents). `patent`, `trend`, `academic_report`: omit it, their ids already are record ids. Omit it for company and person only when you hold record ids.

fields.description: Return only these record fields. Omit for a compact default set; ask for more by name.
